articles.title: Cyclone Arnab aftermath: Central team to visit Odisha today, assess damage
articles.description: A central team will arrive in Odisha on Monday to assess the damage caused by Cyclone Arnab in Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal districts. The team’s findings, along with the State Government’s preliminary damage report, will be sent to the Centre to determine the financial assistance required for the state. The team will be led by Ravi Shankar, Joint Secretary in the Union Ministry of Home Affairs. Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said the Centre would consider both reports before deciding on assistance. He also said the state could use the supplementary budget if required. Central Team To Assess Damage The team includes Man Singh, Director of the Directorate of Rice Development, Patna; Rahul Chaurasia, Deputy Director in the Department of Expenditure, Union Ministry of Finance; Dilip Kumar Jena, Director of the Central Water Commission, Bhubaneswar; Karan Sarin, Deputy Director of the Central Electricity Authority under the Ministry of Power; Sunil Kumar, Superintending Engineer in the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Bhubaneswar; Ajay Kumar Sahu, Under Secretary in the Ministry of Rural Development; and C. Sai Krishna, a scientist at the National Remote Sensing Centre of ISRO, Hyderabad. Majhi said that he had also discussed the cyclone-related damage with Union Home Minister Amit Shah. The assistance package may be reviewed after the final assessment. “We will also send the preliminary damage report to the Central Government, following which the central team will examine it. After the team arrives, assesses the damage and discusses the State Government’s report, central assistance will definitely be provided based on the final report,” the Chief Minister said. Odisha Reviews Cyclone Murasu Preparedness Meanwhile, the state administration is also keeping a close watch on the possible impact of Cyclone Murasu. Majhi visited the office of the Special Relief Commissioner (SRC) yesterday to review the preparations. Officials and rescue teams deployed in the affected areas will remain there, while an additional 50 officers have been deployed to support the response. Relief And Restoration Remain Priorities The Chief Minister said the Government’s immediate focus was on providing timely assistance to people affected by Cyclone Arnab and restoring damaged infrastructure. Efforts are also under way to restore normal life in the affected areas. The state is continuing its response to the damage caused by Arnab while keeping its preparedness in place for the possible impact of Murasu.
